items.name: theme-switch
items.title: Theme Switch
items.description: A theme toggle that rains, drips or sets off fireworks to change the theme.
items.docs:
Theme Switch — A theme toggle that rains, drips or sets off fireworks to change the theme.

The stylesheet sits next to the component and is imported by it, so keep the two together in components/pinui/.

It is set in the system's own UI face, so there is no font to load.

It comes in two themes: pass theme="dark" for the dark one, or wire the prop to your own theme switch.

theme-switch-engine.ts is every effect and must sit beside the component. The component switches its own scene; pass onThemeChange to switch your app's theme when the effect lands, and theme to keep the scene in step with your own switch (a change from outside lands at once). Every effect stays inside the component's box, so give it the room you want the rain and the fireworks to fill, or pass fill. Mark any extra control with data-pts-target and it takes the new theme as the flood reaches it. Diwali's sounds are synthesised with Web Audio and only play after a press; pass sound={false} to silence them. With reduced motion it switches at once.

items.name: reader-card
items.title: Reader Card
items.description: A story card that scrolls in place and morphs into a liquid-glass reader.
items.docs:
Reader Card — A story card that scrolls in place and morphs into a liquid-glass reader.

The stylesheet sits next to the component and is imported by it, so keep the two together in components/pinui/.

It is drawn in Newsreader (variable, with its optical-size axis, and italic) for the titles and the reader, Times New Roman for the card's excerpt (Tinos where it is missing) and Inter for the small labels. The stylesheet reads --font-newsreader and --font-tinos when they are set, as next/font sets them, and otherwise falls back to faces named "Newsreader" and "Tinos". If your project does not already load that face it will fall back to your system sans and look noticeably different.

It comes in two themes: pass theme="dark" for the dark one, or wire the prop to your own theme switch.

reader-card-glass.ts is the liquid glass and must sit beside the component. The full refraction is a backdrop-filter: url() SVG filter, which only Chromium renders; Safari and Firefox get a frosted glass with the same baked rim light on their own. The reader opens inside the scene rather than over your page, so give the scene the room you want the panel to take, or pass fill. If something floats over its foot, set --prc-inset-bottom on a parent to keep the panel above it. Its story is built in: swap the text in ReaderCard.tsx for your own, keeping the excerpt's first passage and the marked lines in step with the card's.

items.name: search-card
items.title: Search Card
items.description: A centred search bar that rises and morphs open into a card of recent searches.
items.docs:
Search Card — A centred search bar that rises and morphs open into a card of recent searches.

The stylesheet sits next to the component and is imported by it, so keep the two together in components/pinui/.

It is drawn in Inter (400 to 600). If your project does not already load that face it will fall back to your system sans and look noticeably different.

It comes in two themes: pass theme="dark" for the dark one, or wire the prop to your own theme switch.

It listens for ⌘K / Ctrl K on the whole window while it is mounted; pass shortcut={false} if your app already uses that key. It keeps the room the open card needs — the bar rests in the middle of it and rises to the top as the card opens — so give it that height rather than overlaying it on content. A press outside closes it — anything marked data-keep-open (a theme switch, say) is left alone.

items.name: desk-computer
items.title: Desk Computer
items.description: A late-90s desk computer in true isometric that you can actually use.
items.docs:
Desk Computer — A late-90s desk computer in true isometric that you can actually use.

The stylesheet sits next to the component and is imported by it, so keep the two together in components/pinui/.

It is drawn in the system UI face for its corners, with Arial drawn into the screen and the badges. If your project does not already load that face it will fall back to your system sans and look noticeably different.

It comes in two themes: pass theme="dark" for the dark one, or wire the prop to your own theme switch.

The drawing is not part of this package: it is ~480KB of SVG, fetched at mount from `src` (default /library/desk-computer.svg). Copy it from https://github.com/shadcn-labs/Pin-UI/tree/main/public/library/desk-computer.svg into your own public folder, or point `src` at wherever you serve it. desk-computer-engine.ts is everything it does and must sit beside the component. Its sounds are synthesised with Web Audio and only ever answer the visitor's own input; pass sound={false} to silence them. It was built with the Anatomy skill's kit (MIT, © 2026 Ryan): https://github.com/wheresryan22/anatomy

items.name: liquid-voice
items.title: Liquid Voice
items.description: A voice-input pill of real liquid glass that stretches into a recorder.
items.docs:
Liquid Voice — A voice-input pill of real liquid glass that stretches into a recorder.

The stylesheet sits next to the component and is imported by it, so keep the two together in components/pinui/.

It is set in the system's own UI face, so there is no font to load.

It comes in two themes: pass theme="dark" for the dark one, or wire the prop to your own theme switch.

The glass is drawn in WebGL 2; without it the component falls back to a CSS gradient and backdrop-filter glass on its own. There is no microphone: the waveform is generated. Wire onSend and onCancel to your own recorder if you need real audio. Pass fill to have the sky take its container's whole box.

items.name: file-box
items.title: File Box
items.description: A cardboard file box whose folders lift out by their tabs.
items.docs:
File Box — A cardboard file box whose folders lift out by their tabs.

The stylesheet sits next to the component and is imported by it, so keep the two together in components/pinui/.

It is set in the system's own UI face, so there is no font to load.

It comes in two themes: pass theme="dark" for the dark one, or wire the prop to your own theme switch.

Its colours are registered as typed CSS custom properties (@property) so a theme change cross-fades; a browser without @property simply switches instantly. Pass fill to have it take its container's whole box, with the scene centred in the largest square that fits.

items.name: copy-paste-pad
items.title: Copy Paste Pad
items.description: A 3-D aluminium macro pad whose ⌘C and ⌘V copy and paste the theme.
items.docs:
Copy Paste Pad — A 3-D aluminium macro pad whose ⌘C and ⌘V copy and paste the theme.

The stylesheet sits next to the component and is imported by it, so keep the two together in components/pinui/.

It is drawn in Inter (400 and 500) for the overlays, with Varela Round for the keycap legends (Arial Rounded where it is missing). If your project does not already load that face it will fall back to your system sans and look noticeably different.

It comes in two themes: pass theme="dark" for the dark one, or wire the prop to your own theme switch.

It renders with three.js's WebGPU renderer (three 0.186 or newer — earlier WebGPU builds can leave a keycap on stale lighting after the theme changes), falling back to WebGL 2 on its own, and imports three when it mounts. Pass onThemeChange so ⌘V can change your theme. ⌘C and ⌘V are only taken while the pad is hovered or focused.

The stylesheet sits next to the component and is imported by it, so keep the two together in components/pinui/.
